# Accepted independent whole-release D14 review — Forma 3.1.0-rc.3

At 2026-10-25T23:40:26.532Z, I accept D14 for frozen source
`e3f90c4871a9be4e8f25db944479681f9355e560`, tree
`c9fe1a360bc8fad69a84ace448812b0dc85c1ed2`, containing 4,578 tracked blobs.
This is my actual independent whole-release judgment after substantive source
review and authentication of the completed current qualification, including all
328 mutation outcomes. There are no unresolved blocking findings. The bounded
nonblocking limitations and explicitly accepted performance costs below remain.
This decision does not publish a release or waive tagged qualification, actual
RC authentication, active burn-in or final publication requirements. Historical
RC2 acceptance and pre-PIFE d6 mutation results are not substituted for the
current evidence.

## Independence and method

The actual reviewer is OpenAI `gpt-6-astra`, separate session
`01a174d8-d19c-7e63-b064-c5d086f43173`, initialized by an actual `fork_turns:none`
spawn under founder decision L-65. The reviewer did not author the implementation
or edit the release checkout. Source inspection, finite read-only probes and
independent evidence verification were performed throughout the candidate's
evolution. A packaging/release-control child review supplied supporting input;
the whole-release judgment remains with this reviewer.

Public provenance is an explicit minimal projection of authentic JSONL records,
including exact source-line hashes and selected model/session/init metadata.
The original local records remain retained. Instructions, private account data,
encrypted material and private advisory contents are excluded from public
evidence. The author and reviewer projections were each checked against actual
raw source lines; same-model identity is disclosed rather than renamed.

The controlling basis is the delivered v2 design, intake and accepted decisions,
including L-50, L-60 through L-67, the later bounded startup policy and the
founder's explicitly authorized 3.1 performance tradeoffs. The review includes
the original 3.1 signal/security work and all integrated runtime, compiler,
server and release-control changes. It is not a diff-only or test-only review.

## Whole implementation assessment

**Native-first rendering and public boundaries.** The compiler's admitted native
subset fails explicitly outside its contract; native FMIR consumes original
source rather than compiler-generated client-template markup. Declared typed
props, the first head state envelope, bounded decoding, schema projection and
deep pollution-key removal preserve the server-to-island boundary. Activation
snapshots original hosts and identity, prepares before commit, makes no initial
repair and preserves early user input. Explicit Browser replacement is a
separate declared mode. Failed islands remain isolated. The native public
response carries the nonce, CSP and no-store together, with named unchecked
exits rather than an implicit unprotected response.

**Lists, ownership and cleanup.** Both reconciliation paths now use SameValueZero
for NaN and signed zero, while owner records are keyed by actual row nodes so
duplicate keys cannot overwrite another occurrence's owner. Rerendered records
move to their replacement node; removal and parent teardown release the correct
owners. Setup failures, synchronous disposal and work registered during teardown
retain explicit cleanup. The existing multirow partial-render exception recovery
limit is still FORMA-298; dispose/remount is the recovery boundary. It is not
represented as repaired, and the retained focused evidence shows no parent
effect leak. The actual 26 ownership regressions and old-source failing controls
provide focused evidence beyond generic suite success.

**Client-template compiler and build pipeline.** `clientTemplates:true` is an
explicit opt-in and defaults off. Eligibility is conservative: known imported
construction, closed element/attribute forms and supported row expressions;
unsupported forms retain ordinary construction. Static structure caching and
staged bindings preserve the reviewed evaluation order. Delegated handlers have
revocation and release their shared document listener when the last owner is
gone; reconnected stale nodes cannot revive them. Their documented propagation
semantics are an opt-in contract, not a claim of native-listener equivalence.
Adopted lists always use adoption, including later rows. The build refuses
missing/incompatible explicit compiler support before writing output. Main and
compiled package entries share owner state and the public export inventory is
now accurate.

**Startup repair.** Exactly five named function expressions replace declarations
in `dom/adoption.ts`: prepareAdoption and its construct/walk/at/visit helpers.
Reversing only these wrappers and the purpose comment recovers the old source
bytes. Function bodies are unchanged. The full source graph and initialization
order show no new premature read across the adoption/activate cycle; actual
fresh packed ESM/CJS consumers in both entry orders hydrate and dispose. The
real production outputs preserve the five parenthesized forms, source maps bind
the reviewed source, and the unchanged startup-source classifier accepts the
actual generated modules. This is generic startup-path code, not a benchmark
route branch. It adds nine gzip bytes; broad whole-file hints were diagnostic
only. Local mixed results and heap observations were retained, not promoted to
hosted qualification or discarded after favorable samples.

**Security/runtime admission.** The review covered the expression allowlist and
precharge order, thrown native errors, URL and attribute context checks, SVG
animation values, explicit mount grants, opaque-origin unreviewed content and
post-parse/post-write stripping. Raw constructors remain trusted-input exits,
not sanitizers. The native renderer checks bounded output/iteration limits and
returns typed faults without intentional process termination. The documented
L-50 content-dependent native-call and per-event budget residuals remain;
neither this release nor the measured hostile corpus establishes universal
50 ms bounds for every possible expression. FMIR structural fuzzing does not
authenticate module producers: modules remain trusted own-build inputs.

**FMIR, packages and release controls.** Writer compatibility requires the same
major and no newer writer minor; patch/prerelease suffixes do not silently change
the binary contract. Ambiguous or incompatible resolved native dependencies are
refused. All seven package versions are coordinated, prerelease peer admission
is exact, public exports are intentional and private imports remain denied.
Scriptless candidate packing, canonical locks, temporary template staging with
restoration, nested artifact hash/path protections, real producer/attempt
identity and immutable archive comparison were inspected. Tag-only publishing
requires exact main CI, engines and P17 before isolated credential jobs, without
credentialed build/install/cache steps. A successful validator does not itself
manufacture independent D14 or actual registry publication.

## Current qualification and material limits

- **Packed P17 40239821236, exact 9f53:** authenticated source/packages, 214-member
  performance ZIP and separate seven candidate archives; all 62 controls pass.
  Independent offline replay verified all raw observations, journal inventory,
  source attribution and cleanup. Both original 20-visit routes have zero
  exceptional tasks, zero affected visits and zero excess. Actual complete
  scheduler-containing tasks peak at 42.186 ms for the tenant route and 40.343 ms
  for the 100-island fixture. All forty independent activation/input probes pass,
  with response-after-paint maxima 198.5/389.9 ms. The 17 pre-application browser
  layout tasks remain separately excluded under the reviewed attribution policy;
  whole-page target misses are retained, not relabeled as startup exceptions.
- **Responsiveness policy:** target 50 ms remains. Rare proved startup exceptions
  remain jointly bounded at no more than two tasks, two visits and 10 ms total
  excess per original twenty visits, each at most 55 ms. The successful current
  P17 needs none. L-67 complete-public-set scaling remains distinct from
  individual-edit latency; current engine jobs retained the real absolute guards.
- **Full engines 40239823036:** authenticated checkout/job logs show all three
  engines passed their actual functional, serialized cost, HTML context, indexed
  and complete-public-set controls. Firefox/WebKit parity includes 28 modules,
  118 states and no unexpected divergences. Ordinary CI 40239814838 passed
  19 jobs with its expected registry-scaffold skip; its actual synthetic merge
  producer is disclosed and tree-equivalent to 9f53.
- **Security/expression/hostile evidence:** authenticated current artifacts show
  six Rust security mutants killed with before/restored controls, 100,000
  expression cases before and after with a caught negative control, and 2,082
  hostile cases plus 30 cap controls with a caught guard mutant. Raw subsets,
  overlaps, actual producer identity and restoration limits remain explicit.
  They are separate from the now-authenticated current full 328 campaign below.
- **FMIR/SR14 scope:** the retained 246/346-file closures remain unchanged through
  Y, with original exact producers and finite results. Four 1,201-second ASan
  fuzz targets qualify their recorded execution; truncated historical progress
  logs and an unarchived evolving cache/corpus are explicit limits.
- **Corrected native resource run 40235112915:** actual local prerelease crate
  resolution and unchanged external lock graph are proven after discovering and
  repairing unused local patches in the original harness. Qualified resource
  values are 4.293333 MiB, 13.533441 ms boot remainder and 78,188,929 B image,
  within 8 MiB / 50 ms / 150 MB. The fixture combines current Rust with frozen
  published npm inputs. It is not claimed to be a whole-RC3 image. The invalid
  earlier identity run remains retained with no current-resource credit.
- **Bytes:** all five current package caps pass, including main 49,845/49,926 B;
  the tight normally built Forma route is 28,238/28,420 B. Other caps are not
  raised or exchanged. The approved core cap is separate from the route cap and
  the original v2 targets; the original targets are not all declared met.
- **Current Linux 40240214599:** all 1,305 samples were authenticated and the
  reported means, spreads and geometric means independently recomputed. Against
  8ae, signals overall is 4.89% lower, fan-out 13.11% lower, diamond 11.29% lower
  and effect create/dispose 8.79% lower. Control movement and individual values
  remain visible; unchanged reactive chunks do not prove absence of an observed
  regression. Current original target ratios include write 89.42% and overall
  87.95% passing, fan 74.51% and effect create/dispose 79.46% missing, and keyed
  row edit 1.563x missing its 1.1x goal. DOM bytes are identical between candidates
  but measured DOM geometric mean is 1.56% lower, with absolute costs recorded.
  The current startup evidence supports the founder's explicit documented
  acceptance of these bounded measured costs. No equivalence, noise, universal
  speedup, favorable rerun or automatic inherited waiver is claimed.
- **Dependency alerts:** all 86 current open alerts map to historical snapshots
  or separate benchmark competitor locks. The shipped seven-package inventory,
  current source/lock checks and production CI advisory gates establish no new
  affected shipped Forma dependency. The competitor runtime alerts remain real,
  visible maintenance work outside this release's dependency scope.

## Findings and final dispositions

The compiler-export inventory omission (D14-RC3-001) is resolved in the frozen
source. The invalid current native-resource identity (D14-RC3-004) is resolved by
the strict consumer-resolution repair and authenticated corrected run. The
FORMA-299 startup qualification failure is resolved by the reviewed five-PIFE
candidate and actual fresh packed P17 evidence. FORMA-298 remains an explicitly
bounded nonblocking historical limitation. Current material performance costs
and original target misses remain accepted, disclosed product tradeoffs rather
than falsely passing targets. The dependency banner introduces no new shipped
blocker within the independently checked scope.

D14-RC3-002 is resolved by authenticated current full mutation run 40239819395,
attempt 1, actual 9f53 source. Independent provider metadata and complete approved
checkout/command logs bind the original 10,232,365-byte ZIP, artifact 12618510708,
SHA-256 `e24750461e6a51fd15ba8546ddb3dbda2b047aa89083a575dda06921cf4219c7`.
All 993 members pass integrity/path/type checks. A separate independent Python
implementation checks every raw report/process/log triple, exact corpus order,
completed assertion, baseline identity, cancellation and failure classification;
the primary analyst's exact committed-classifier replay independently agrees.
All 328 execute: 326 caught, two survived, zero equivalent and zero unqualified.
Overall 99.3902439% and expressions 98/98 pass the unchanged 85% floors; all
169 security probes are caught. Both baselines pass 4,294 tests with identical
identities/states, and all 26 ownership controls pass in both baselines and both
survivor runs. The two threshold survivors remain counted. Their obsolete NaN
notes are tracked in FORMA-300, without corpus rewrite or equivalence exemption.
Historical 40232848552 failed before mutants; historical 40233270424 qualifies
d6 only. Neither failure nor producer identity is erased.

The restored baseline and exact harness restoration path support source cleanup;
no absent archived final hash of every restored file is invented. Campaign
elapsed time is not a controlled performance comparison. All 35 mutation target
files and the actual mutation workflow match from 9f53 through Y. The complete
frozen-Y diff identifies only six factual edits. Core CHANGELOG is a changed
docs-truth input, not a byte-identical input: current Y CI 40242614339 supplies
19 successful jobs and the expected registry-scaffold skip, with actual
Node24 logs showing all 20 core docs-truth controls pass. Its actual synthetic
producer `48713faebc87e82fe6c3ea675194198537ffb3c0` has exactly Y's tree, proved by
both Git commit tree objects. This qualifies the factual test-input delta without
relabeling the producer or asserting whole-archive equality.

## Frozen Y and release boundary

The Y manifest SHA-256 is
`7f327838edc4bb24a1aa0a1b180d805dbe49fbca3774bfe1a653441d1843b688`.
Only six previously reviewed factual files differ from 9f53, with exact hashes
matched. The sole contract change is the FORMA-259 scope description; all gate
statuses and limits remain unchanged. Current product source and test/build/workflow files
are unchanged; the factual core CHANGELOG test-input delta is separately
validated by Y CI as described above. Packed core CHANGELOG and crate VCS metadata prevent a claim of
whole-archive identity. Exact tagged packaging, P17 and publication evidence must
be authenticated separately.

L-60 live identity/protection/alerting deferrals remain actual residuals; source
CODEOWNERS and workflow tests are not proof of live actor separation. After an
accepted D14, RC authentication and at least 3,600 active zero-fault packed-RC
burn-in seconds remain required before final publication. The historical 3.0
quota exception does not waive 3.1's gates. Final prepared docs/version changes
must remain within the independently reviewed canonical transition; current
registry and immutable artifact checks remain mandatory. Private security
publication sequencing is preserved without disclosing draft contents here.

No source edit, heavy campaign, public GitHub approval, merge, tag or publication
was performed by this reviewer. This document is the actual accepted D14 review,
with its own evidence hash; the source and review-evidence validators only check
the resulting binding and do not create the substantive decision.

The separately inspected three post-Y factual documentation edits record actual
mutation/Y-CI results and preserve all remaining release prerequisites. They
contain no product, test, workflow, threshold or gate-status change and fit the
existing documentation allowance. Their actual committed binding still must be
validated. No future unreviewed documentation or source change is accepted here.
